back: The Intertropical Convergence Zone: where the trade winds from the two hemispheres meet, air rises and heavy rain falls. It moves north and south with the overhead Sun, lagging by several weeks.
Within about 10° of the equator: about 25–28 °C all year, an annual range under 3 °C, more than 2 000 mm of rain and no dry season.
About 5°–20° from the equator: high temperatures, one wet and one dry season, annual rainfall about 600–1 500 mm and an annual temperature range of about 5–10 °C.

front: Cause of the savanna dry season
back: The ITCZ moves away and the subtropical anticyclone brings sinking, stable air, so cloud does not form.
A seasonal reversal of the prevailing wind. In summer it brings moist air from the sea and heavy rain; in winter it brings dry air from the land.
El Niño–Southern Oscillation: a natural variation in the tropical Pacific with a warm phase (El Niño) and a cool phase (La Niña) that changes rainfall worldwide every few years.
El Niño tends to bring a dry rainy season to southern Africa; the 2015–16 and 2023–24 events were followed by serious drought.

front: Diurnal and annual range in the rainforest
back: The range between day and night (about 5–10 °C) is greater than the range between the warmest and coolest months (under 3 °C).
Share (%) = rainfall in the season ÷ annual total × 100.
